root.name: Petrov's Defense: Moody Gambit
root.moves: 1. e4 e5 2. Nf3 Nf6 3. Qe2 Nc6 4. d4

overview: White defends e4 with 3.Qe2 and then pushes 4.d4 to open the centre with a lead in development, offering the e-pawn exchange. Black can take on d4 or play ...Nxe4 and often gets an acceptable game, but the white queen on the e-file makes the opening awkward for both. It is an unusual sideline, not a main line.

white_ideas.idea: Open the centre fast with d4
Use the e-file and the queen on e2 for pressure

black_ideas.idea: Take on d4 and develop with ...Be7 and ...O-O
Hit e4 with ...Nxe4 when it works

typical_structures.structure: Open centre with pawns traded on d4
Queen on e2 against Black knights

character.notes: Open and tactical, with the queen early and pins on the e-file.

gambit.notes: The d4 pawn is defended and material stays level or comes straight back.

soundness.notes: Black has several simple answers, so White gets little.

structure.notes: The d- and e-pawns are exchanged early, opening lines.

approach.notes: Rare for strong players, who prefer 3.Nxe5 or 3.d4.

character.reason: The early queen and open centre make moves forcing.

gambit.reason: Despite the name no pawn is lost for good; the d4 push keeps material level.

soundness.reason: It does no real harm to either side.

structure.reason: Pawns come off in the centre and the e-file opens.

level.reason: The play is easy to follow but not a first repertoire choice.

plans.reason: White tries to use the queen early and a lead in development.
